correctness.rationale: Exact diagonalization makes the centered Gaussian-probe risk 2S(k)/N, where S(k) is the squared logarithmic spectral tail. The adjacent ratio assumption yields the termwise shift S(k+h)<=q^(2h) S(k), establishing the global budget inequality; N<=2^(N-1) proves the stated sufficient q bound. Finite geometric matrices with B=2c prove necessity. Exact adjacent risk ratios resolve all geometric optimizers and ties; the integral test and compact-interior optimization yield the polynomial limit and constant. A standalone stdlib program passed 7,205 checks; finite computation is not used as an infinite proof. The trace-class infinite examples use convergent Gaussian series, not non-existent Hilbert-valued standard Gaussians.

A comparison by implication found no matching sharp uniform adjacent-log-decay threshold across all finite dimensions and budgets, nor its necessity witness and geometric-versus-polynomial allocation classification, in inspected primary text or accessible mathematical records. The claim is restricted to the ideal spectral-deflation estimator, not practical Nyström or unrestricted trace estimation. Residual unindexed or incompletely read literature may contain related or dominating claims.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating study explicitly asks how to allocate computation between rank of a preconditioner and number of trace probes. The exact dimension-independent q frontier and finite necessity example give a mathematically falsifiable allocation rule for an entire natural spectral class, not an arbitrary slice. The explicit closed geometric optimizer and polynomial fractional split demonstrate a substantive change of resource-allocation regime with decay type. The quantified theorem clarifies the ideal limit of one-probe recommendations, while not claiming practical Nyström performance.
